findings.body: NullPointerException is thrown from getCredentials(), breaking any caller that enumerates federated credentials (e.g. account REST credential listing) for the affected user.
findings.failure_mode: Uncaught NullPointerException on credential enumeration for an unmatched/uninitialized federated user.
findings.impact: NullPointerException is thrown from getCredentials(), breaking any caller that enumerates federated credentials (e.g. account REST credential listing) for the affected user.
findings.root_cause: New getCredentials() override omits the null-check pattern applied consistently to MyUser lookups elsewhere in this class.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same `if (myUser == null) return Stream.empty();` guard used in getDisableableCredentialTypesStream/isConfiguredFor before dereferencing myUser.
findings.title: getCredentials() dereferences MyUser without the null-guard used elsewhere in the class
findings.trigger: getCredentials(realm, user) is invoked (e.g. via credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()/getCredentials()) for a user whose entry is not present in the internal `users` map (getMyUser returns null), a situation the sibling methods isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream both explicitly guard against.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R232 assigns `var myUser = getMyUser(user)` and R235 immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` without null-checking myUser. Other methods in this class (e.g., isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) guard against null myUser. If getMyUser returns null for an unknown user, NPE will be thrown.

raw_findings.body: Unlike the local-storage path (which calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode()/updateStoredCredential after a successful match), this federated implementation performs a stateless membership check and never removes the consumed code, so a single recovery code can be reused indefinitely, defeating the one-time-use guarantee the feature is meant to test.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Recovery codes become reusable, silently invalidating the one-time-use security property being validated by tests using this storage provider.
raw_findings.impact: Unlike the local-storage path (which calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode()/updateStoredCredential after a successful match), this federated implementation performs a stateless membership check and never removes the consumed code, so a single recovery code can be reused indefinitely, defeating the one-time-use guarantee the feature is meant to test.
raw_findings.root_cause: New isValid() branch for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE performs only a read-only equality check with no follow-up mutation of stored credential state.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After a successful match, remove the used code from the stored list (re-serialize and persist the remaining codes) or otherwise track/mark consumption, mirroring RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid()'s removeRecoveryAuthnCode() behavior.
raw_findings.title: Federated recovery-code validation never removes/marks used codes, allowing infinite reuse
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user authenticates twice with the same recovery code once this storage provider's isValid() (CredentialInputValidator) is the one that services the credential (bypassing RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider's own consume/remove logic).

raw_findings.body: Recovery codes are stored in plaintext in the (test) federated store instead of hashed as done for the local DB path (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues hashes each code), establishing an insecure at-rest storage pattern for this credential type.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Sensitive one-time recovery codes are stored in plaintext, undermining the security property the hashed local-storage path enforces.
raw_findings.impact: Recovery codes are stored in plaintext in the (test) federated store instead of hashed as done for the local DB path (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues hashes each code), establishing an insecure at-rest storage pattern for this credential type.
raw_findings.root_cause: New RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE branch in updateCredential() stores the raw challenge response verbatim instead of hashing it before persistence.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Hash each recovery code (e.g. via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode) before persisting credentialData, and compare hashed values during isValid(), consistent with local storage handling.
raw_findings.title: Recovery codes persisted unhashed in federated user storage unlike hashed local storage
raw_findings.trigger: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() routes a federated user's recovery codes to updateCredential(), and this provider persists the raw challengeResponse (the plaintext generated codes) directly as credentialData, with no hashing step, unlike password storage which is hashed via a PasswordHashProvider in this same class.

raw_findings.body: The returned RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel has a null id, which can break any downstream code (account REST listing, credential removal by id, UI dedup logic) that expects a non-null credential id for federated credentials.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Federated recovery-codes credentials surface with a null identifier, risking NPEs or broken identification in consumers of getCredentials().
raw_findings.impact: The returned RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel has a null id, which can break any downstream code (account REST listing, credential removal by id, UI dedup logic) that expects a non-null credential id for federated credentials.
raw_findings.root_cause: The recovery-codes credential construction path reuses createFromValues(), which by design does not set an id, and the caller does not compensate by assigning one as was done for OTP.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Call model.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()) (or a stable derived id) on the model returned from createFromValues() before adding it to credentialModels, mirroring the OTP fix in the same method.
raw_findings.title: Recovery-codes credential model returned by getCredentials() has no ID unlike the OTP model
raw_findings.trigger: getCredentials() is called and the recovery-codes branch builds its CredentialModel via createFromValues(), which never assigns an id, whereas the OTP branch just above it was fixed in this same patch to call newOTP.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()).
